reason: The remaining blood-side goal names the capillaries and the vein to the liver.
expectation: The capillaries will join the vein to make a route carrying blood toward the liver.

reason: The remaining goal is to bring the folded lining and blood route close together.
expectation: The capillaries will sit close to the thin lining so food molecules can cross into the blood.

effect: The completed surface shows glucose and amino acids crossing the thin lining into nearby capillaries, with blood carrying them toward the liver. All goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the two sides form one route from the gut toward the liver.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the lining and blood route was most worthwhile: it connected the folds and thin walls to how absorbed food reaches the blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the blood route was clear but fairly predictable because the goal named both pieces.

surprise.text: The flattened comparison helped me see how folds can fit more surface into the lining.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; the goals and pictures gave each pairing a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would try another chapter because putting the two sides together made the connection between digestion and blood transport understandable, though the individual pairings were mostly predictable.
